title: Thread a shock cord through a spring cord lock, pressing its button to open it
instruction: Press in the button of the black cord lock and keep it pressed in, with no more than 2 mm of it standing out, from before the white shock cord's end goes in until that end is through the lock's hole. Push the end through until at least 4 cm of cord sticks out of the far side, with at least 4 cm left on the near side. Finish with the lock resting on the table, gripping the cord by its spring alone, and both grippers clear of the lock and the cord.
context: Spring cord locks close the drawcords of hoods, jacket hems and backpacks, and come with no-tie shoelaces, whose fitting guide says to press the lock and thread the lace ends with the other hand. Most people have squeezed one; when the cord slips out, threading it back is that squeeze, held while the other hand feeds the cord. Hardest ability: the passage admits the 7.9 mm cord only while the button is held at least 3.5 mm in (5.25 N), with 1.75 mm per side only at flush (7 mm, 10.5 N), and the squeeze that opens the loose 8.8 g lock also holds it. The end must pass 13 mm deep and come 40 mm out: pushed in one go, at least 53 mm of cord is free and buckles at 0.9 N or less. Nearest: TK-462BUT holds a plumbing collet's release while a rigid pipe moves through it; TK-UC3UAQ passes a cable through a grommet. Here: a garment cord lock, a soft cord, and an end state read from the spring, the plunger held in by the cord alone.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. The layout is the same in every trial; nothing is hidden and nothing is fixed to the table. Both arms start at their ready pose. CORD LOCK (loose): a Ravenox Extra Large spring cord lock, black Delrin (acetal) with a stainless steel spring. Catalogue size 1.6 x 0.8 x 0.5 in. (41 x 20 x 13 mm with the button out), hole 0.65 x 0.45 in. (16.5 x 11.4 mm), the 11.4 mm along the lock's length. Body 34 x 20 x 13 mm: two 2 mm faces with the catalogue hole, 2 mm top and bottom walls and a closed end, leaving a 9 x 16 mm open end; hole centre 15 mm from the closed end, midway across. Plunger: 28.5 x 16 x 9 mm, filling the open end; its last 7 mm stands out of the body as the button. Its own hole is 11.4 x 13 mm. The spring holds the plunger out with its hole 7 mm off the body's, so the passage through the lock is 4.4 mm wide; pressing the button in by q widens it to 4.4 mm + q. Flush (7 mm in; the body's end face is the stop) the holes line up: a passage 11.4 x 13 mm through the 13 mm depth. Spring 1.5 N/mm from the free position (10.5 N at flush). Masses from the solid volumes at 1.41 g/cm3: body 4.9 g, plunger 3.9 g, 8.8 g in all. Start: lying on one 34 x 13 mm side, button toward +x, hole axis along y, body centre at x 302, y 130 (closed end at x 285, button end at x 326). SHOCK CORD (loose): 320 mm of 5/16 in. (7.9 mm) polyester-covered rubber shock cord, white with a black tracer (Tarpsnow TA-UC-SC3125, about 3.1 lb per 100 ft, 46 g/m), 14.7 g, both ends heat-sealed round when cut, no aglet. Bending stiffness 0.001 N m2: 60 mm held level droops 0.7 mm. Three pen rings on each end, 5, 23 and 53 mm from the end, for reading a real trial. Start: straight along y at x 300 on the table, one end at y -60 pointing to +y, the other at y -380. Simulation: the cord is 16 capsules of 20 mm (radius 3.95 mm, 16-sided collider) on bending joints of 0.05 N m/rad, friction 0.6, no stretch. The lock's body and plunger are built from boxes, edges square instead of rounded; the plunger slides on a prismatic joint, 0 to 7 mm, with the spring above; friction 0.4. Real build: the named lock and a 320 mm length of the named cord; the lock's own plunger and spring are the simulated joint. For reading: a steel rule and a caliper.
scoring: Read every step from the cord's centre line (two ends, 16 segment centres), the lock's pose and the plunger's travel. The scoring window is the body hole's outline (11.4 x 16.5 mm), which contains the 11.4 x 13 mm passage, across the lock's 13 mm depth. The cord is through when its centre line crosses the lock's mid-plane inside that window exactly once (a 7.9 mm cord fits only once). Out, for each side: the length of cord, measured along the cord, from where it first reaches that side's face to its end on that side; the cord's out is the smaller of the two sides. In: how far a cord end lying inside the window is from the face it entered by. Released: every point of both grippers' finger zones (pad thickness and width included) is at least 30 mm from the lock and the cord; unreadable arms count as not released. Let go: released on every step of the last 1 s (20 steps). Pressed: at some step while no cord end was 5 mm in and the cord was not through, the plunger was at least 5 mm in (the button at most 2 mm out), and it stays at least 5 mm in on every step from the first step a cord end is 5 mm in until the cord is first through; a wedged cord end pushes it only 3.5 mm in, so every line above 0 needs Pressed, and 0.5 and up need the press held (a press lost leaves 0.25 at most). The score is the highest line that holds: 1.0 (success; the trial ends once it has held 1 s): let go, and on every step of that second, all at once: the cord through with out at least 40 mm; the lock resting on the table (its lowest point within 2 mm of the table top); the plunger held at least 1 mm in from its free position (the button at most 6 mm out; with nothing in the hole it springs back to 7 mm out); no point of the lock or the cord moving more than 2 mm in that second. 0.75: let go, and the cord through with out at least 40 mm. 0.5: let go, and the cord through with out at least 10 mm. 0.25: at some point in the trial a cord end was at least 5 mm in (with the button out the 4.4 mm passage stops the 7.9 mm cord within 3 mm); a held cord or lock earns at most this. 0: anything else. Doing nothing scores 0 (no whole-trial zero). Why the plunger reading is the grip: with both grippers clear only the cord can hold the plunger in, and held 1 mm or more in, the spring presses it with 1.5 N or more, a friction hold 17 times the lock's 0.086 N weight. Real trial: the top video shows the button at most 2 mm out before the 5 mm ring reaches the entry face and for as long as the cord end is in the lock until it is through, until the end is past the lock's middle (Pressed held); the pen rings 5, 23 and 53 mm from the threaded end (5 mm in; 13 + 10 and 13 + 40 mm along the cord) are read on the side video: the 5 mm ring at or past the entry face for 0.25, the 23 mm ring for 0.5, the 53 mm ring for 0.75 and 1.0; a steel rule checks the near side; the depth rod of a caliper on the button (6 mm or less out) reads the plunger; the top video shows the grippers 30 mm clear (a 30 mm card) and 1 s still; the side video shows the lock on the table.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz, control 20 Hz. Simplified: the spring is a prismatic joint, 1.5 N/mm, no preload; the cord is 16 rigid 20 mm capsules on bending joints, without stretch or flattening, so it holds the button 3.5 mm out (a squashed real cord sits further out; the 6 mm limit passes one squashed to 5.4 mm); square edges; solid masses. The lock's walls and hole position, the plunger's size, hole, travel, the spring rate and the cord's stiffness are our estimates. Not modelled: braid texture.
reset_notes: Press the button, pull the cord back out of the lock and let the button spring out (it stands 7 mm out). Lay the lock on a long side with its body centre at x 302, y 130, button toward +x, hole axis along y. Lay the cord straight along y at x 300 with one end at y -60 pointing to +y. Check that the pen rings can be read.
